claim: The Ex8 mutant lacks any cytoplasmic domains and consequently is distributed through the ER.
source: These data are consistent with our understanding of TANGO1 function, as its cytoplasmic domains are required to recruit TANGO1 to ERES. The Ex8 mutant lacks any cytoplasmic domains and consequently is distributed through the ER.
evidence: This is stated in the results section as an interpretation of the localization data.

claim: A stable U2OS cell line expressing Ex8-HA under a constitutive promoter was generated.
source: For this purpose, a stable U2OS cell line expressing Ex8-HA under a constitutive promoter was generated and compared with control cells by microscopy.
evidence: This is stated in the results section describing the experimental approach.

claim: Cells expressing Ex8-HA showed weaker and more diffuse staining of collagen I compared with control cells.
source: Cells expressing Ex8-HA showed weaker and more diffuse staining of collagen I compared with control cells (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A.

claim: qRT-PCR analyses confirmed that collagen I expression is reduced in the Ex8-HA stable cell line.
source: To confirm that this reduction was not due to unequal immunofluorescent staining, total RNA was isolated from the two cell populations and the relative amount of collagen I/GAPDH transcript was quantified by qRT-PCR analyses (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B). This confirmed that collagen I expression is reduced in the Ex8-HA stable cell line.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The reduction in collagen I expression was not due to unfolded protein response (UPR) as there was no difference in XBP-1 splicing upon expression of Ex8-HA.
source: The reduction in expression was not due to unfolded protein response (UPR) as there was no difference in XBP-1 splicing upon expression of Ex8-HA (Figure 5—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1C.

claim: A cycloheximide chase experiment was performed to test whether the secretion of collagen I was affected.
source: The next step was to test whether the secretion of collagen I was also affected. Since different rates of collagen synthesis will affect the amount available for secretion in the two cell populations, a cycloheximide chase experiment was performed (Figure 5).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 5.

claim: A drastic reduction in the rate of collagen I secretion from the EX8-HA stable cell line compared to control cells was observed.
source: By quantifying the relative amount of collagen I present in the cells and in the media at each time point, a drastic reduction in the rate of collagen I secretion from the EX8-HA stable cell line compared to control cells was observed.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 5.

claim: The effect on collagen I secretion was not due to a general reduction of protein secretion since the small cargo antitrypsin was produced and secreted at a comparable rate in the two cell populations.
source: Importantly, this effect was not due to a general reduction of protein secretion since the small cargo antitrypsin was produced and secreted at a comparable rate in the two cell populations.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 5.

claim: Six independent trials revealed a consistent trend of a net reduction in secretion of collagen IV and collagen XII in the EX8-HA stable line.
source: Under the same conditions, we tested secretion of collagen IV and collagen XII in EX8-HA stable line. Six independent trials revealed a consistent trend of a net reduction in their secretion, but because of the low relative abundance of these collagens the magnitude of the effect varied considerably and cannot be statistically quantified (Figure 5—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2.

claim: No change in collagen I secretion was observed when full-length TANGO1 was overexpressed in U2OS.
source: These secretion defects were specific to Ex8 expression as we observed no change in collagen I secretion when full-length TANGO1 was overexpressed in U2OS (Figure 5—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 3.

claim: Expression of the exon eight skipped splice product even in the presence of full length TANGO1 affects collagen I homeostasis.
source: Collectively, these results show that expression of the exon eight skipped splice product even in the presence of full length TANGO1 affects collagen I homeostasis.
evidence: This is stated in the results section as a conclusion from the experimental data.

claim: Aberrant expression of a truncated TANGO1 protein and/or reduced levels of fully functional TANGO1 protein causes a novel syndrome due to disturbances in cellular protein secretion.
source: Our study provides evidence that aberrant expression of a truncated TANGO1 protein and/or reduced levels of fully functional TANGO1 protein, or likely a combination of both causes a novel syndrome due to disturbances in cellular protein secretion.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a primary conclusion of the study.

claim: The heterozygous parents show exon eight skipping but no detectable symptoms.
source: The heterozygous parents show exon eight skipping but no detectable symptoms, whereas all four homozygous children are severely and similarly affected.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by data in Figures 2 and 3 and Table 1.

claim: All four homozygous children are severely and similarly affected.
source: The heterozygous parents show exon eight skipping but no detectable symptoms, whereas all four homozygous children are severely and similarly affected.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by data in Table 1.

claim: The disease only manifests when the ratio of truncated versus normal protein exceeds a critical level.
source: This is consistent with a threshold model, where the disease only manifests when the ratio of truncated versus normal protein exceeds a critical level.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as an interpretation of the data.

claim: Tango1 knockout mice are defective for the secretion of numerous collagens.
source: Tango1 knockout mice represent a full loss-of-function (LoF) situation and are defective for the secretion of numerous collagens, exhibiting short-limbed dwarfism, compromised chondrocyte maturation and bone mineralization, and other features (Wilson et al., 2011), resembling our patients' phenotype.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by a citation.

claim: Tango1 knockout mice exhibit short-limbed dwarfism, compromised chondrocyte maturation and bone mineralization, and other features.
source: Tango1 knockout mice represent a full loss-of-function (LoF) situation and are defective for the secretion of numerous collagens, exhibiting short-limbed dwarfism, compromised chondrocyte maturation and bone mineralization, and other features (Wilson et al., 2011), resembling our patients' phenotype.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by a citation.

claim: Tango1 knockout mice phenotype resembles the patients' phenotype.
source: Tango1 knockout mice represent a full loss-of-function (LoF) situation and are defective for the secretion of numerous collagens, exhibiting short-limbed dwarfism, compromised chondrocyte maturation and bone mineralization, and other features (Wilson et al., 2011), resembling our patients' phenotype.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as an interpretation.

claim: The human TANGO1 locus lies within a homozygous interval shared among the affected children.
source: The human TANGO1 locus lies within a homozygous interval shared among the affected children, which strengthens its role as the disease-causing gene in the investigated family.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by data in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: TANGO1 does not seem to be haploinsufficient, since there are several heterozygous LoF mutation carriers listed in big population databases.
source: TANGO1 does not seem to be haploinsufficient, since there are several heterozygous LoF mutation carriers listed in big population databases, ExAC and gnomAD (Lek et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by a citation to population databases.

claim: No homozygous LoF mutation carriers have been reported so far in TANGO1.
source: However, no homozygous LoF mutation carriers have been reported so far.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion based on database searches.

claim: Complete ablation of functional TANGO1 may cause embryonic lethality in humans.
source: Thus, complete ablation of functional TANGO1 may cause embryonic lethality in humans.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as speculation based on the absence of homozygous LoF carriers.

claim: The skipped exon eight in full length TANGO1 corresponds to exon three in the isoform TANGO1-short.
source: The skipped exon eight in full length TANGO1 corresponds to exon three in the isoform TANGO1-short.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as an observation about the gene structure.

claim: Exclusion of exon three in TANGO1-short leads to a premature stop codon 27 bp downstream of exon 2.
source: Its exclusion there also leads to a premature stop codon 27 bp downstream of exon 2.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as an inference about the effect on TANGO1-short.

claim: TANGO1-short has been shown to substitute the function of TANGO1 in collagen export, and vice versa.
source: However, TANGO1-short has been shown to substitute the function of TANGO1 in collagen export, and vice versa (Maeda et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by a citation.

claim: The cytoplasmic portion's capacity to recruit ERGIC-53 membranes, Sec23/24 complexes, and cTAGE5 is sufficient to export collagen at the ER.
source: It has been postulated that the cytoplasmic portion's capacity to recruit ERGIC-53 membranes, Sec23/24 complexes, and cTAGE5, shared by both isoforms, is sufficient to export collagen at the ER (Saito et al., 2009; Santos et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by citations.

claim: The lumenal SH3 domain may play a role in modulating the efficiency or the quality (folding status) of collagens to be secreted.
source: The lumenal SH3 domain may therefore rather play a role in modulating the efficiency or the quality (folding status) of collagens to be secreted (Maeda et al., 2016; Raote et al., 2018; Saito et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by citations.

claim: The identified mutation in exon eight does not only compromise the function of TANGO1, but most likely also of TANGO1-short.
source: Since the identified mutation in exon eight does not only compromise the function of TANGO1, but most likely also of TANGO1-short, the short isoform cannot attenuate our patients' phenotype.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as an inference about the mutation's effect.

claim: The short isoform cannot attenuate the patients' phenotype.
source: Since the identified mutation in exon eight does not only compromise the function of TANGO1, but most likely also of TANGO1-short, the short isoform cannot attenuate our patients' phenotype.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as an inference.

claim: The truncated TANGO1 protein is unable to access ERES.
source: The truncated TANGO1 protein is unable to access ERES and is distributed throughout the ER (Figure 4).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by data in Figure 4.

claim: Expression of mutant TANGO1 in cells along with endogenous full length TANGO1 displayed a negative effect on collagen secretion.
source: Its expression in cells along with endogenous full length TANGO1 displayed a negative effect on collagen secretion.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by data in Figure 5.

claim: The effect of mutant TANGO1 is specific to collagen, as the secretion of antitrypsin remains unaffected.
source: This effect is specific to collagen, as the secretion of antitrypsin remains unaffected (Figure 5).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by data in Figure 5.

claim: TANGO1 functions to export all soluble collagens tested thus far, including collagen I.
source: However, it has been demonstrated subsequently that TANGO1 functions to export all soluble collagens tested thus far, including collagen I.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as established knowledge.

claim: There has been a change in the mRNA level of collagen α1 chain in U2OS cells expressing mutant TANGO1.
source: We have noticed a change in the mRNA level of collagen α1 chain in U2OS cells expressing mutant TANGO1.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by data in Figure 5—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Expression of mutant TANGO1 appears not to involve the activation of UPR in U2OS cells.
source: However, this appears not to involve the activation of UPR in U2OS cells.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by data in Figure 5—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Type I collagens provide tensile strength to connective tissue.
source: Type I collagens provide tensile strength to connective tissue and are abundant in bone, skin, dentin, cementum, tendons, and ligaments (Deshmukh et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by a citation.

claim: Type I collagens are abundant in bone, skin, dentin, cementum, tendons, and ligaments.
source: Type I collagens provide tensile strength to connective tissue and are abundant in bone, skin, dentin, cementum, tendons, and ligaments (Deshmukh et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by a citation.

claim: Impaired collagen I secretion may underlie several key symptoms in the patients, in particular the tooth and skeletal abnormalities.
source: Impaired collagen I secretion may underlie several key symptoms in our patients, in particular the tooth and skeletal abnormalities.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as an interpretation of the findings.

claim: Haploinsufficiency or gain of function mutations in COL1A1 and COL1A2 can cause different forms of osteogenesis imperfecta (OI) with or without dentinogenesis imperfecta (DGI).
source: Haploinsufficiency or gain of function mutations in COL1A1 and COL1A2, coding for the pro-collagen I chains, can cause different forms of osteogenesis imperfecta (OI) with (OMIM #259420) or without dentinogenesis imperfecta (DGI).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as established knowledge.

claim: Hearing loss is commonly found in OI patients.
source: Hearing loss is commonly found in OI patients.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as established knowledge.

claim: Mutations in other collagen genes have been associated with hereditary hearing loss.
source: Mutations in other collagen genes, for example COL2A1, COL4A3, COL4A4, COL4A5, COL4A6, COL9A1, COL9A2 and COL9A3, COL11A1, and/or COL11A2 have been associated with hereditary hearing loss (https://hereditaryhearingloss.org/).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by a reference to a database.

claim: TANGO1 may control secretion of cargoes other than collagens.
source: TANGO1 may control secretion of cargoes other than collagens.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as speculation.

claim: TANGO1 has a role in mucin export in Drosophila salivary glands.
source: This is particularly noteworthy based on the recently reported role of TANGO1 in mucin export in Drosophila salivary glands and insulin secretion (Fan et al., 2017; Kang et al., 2019; Reynolds et al., 2019)
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by citations.

claim: TANGO1 has a role in insulin secretion.
source: This is particularly noteworthy based on the recently reported role of TANGO1 in mucin export in Drosophila salivary glands and insulin secretion (Fan et al., 2017; Kang et al., 2019; Reynolds et al., 2019)
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by citations.

claim: The complex phenotype of the patients may at least partially be due to aberrant export and secretion of other proteins in a tissue specific manner.
source: Therefore, the complex phenotype of our patients, including DGI, diabetes, intellectual disability and hearing impairment, but no brittle bones may at least partially be due to aberrant export and secretion of other proteins in a tissue specific manner.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as speculation.

claim: Mutations in the dentin sialophosphoprotein (DSPP) gene may cause DGI 1 with or without hearing loss.
source: For example, mutations in the dentin sialophosphoprotein (DSPP) gene and, by extrapolation, TANGO1-associated defects in DSPP secretion, may cause DGI 1 (#605594) with or without hearing loss (Xiao et al., 2001) as well as DGI, Shields type II (#125490) and III (#125500), which may be phenotypic variation of the same entity rather than separate diseases (Kim et al., 2005).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by citations.

claim: TANGO1-associated defects in DSPP secretion may cause DGI 1 with or without hearing loss.
source: For example, mutations in the dentin sialophosphoprotein (DSPP) gene and, by extrapolation, TANGO1-associated defects in DSPP secretion, may cause DGI 1 (#605594) with or without hearing loss (Xiao et al., 2001) as well as DGI, Shields type II (#125490) and III (#125500), which may be phenotypic variation of the same entity rather than separate diseases (Kim et al., 2005).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as speculation based on extrapolation.

claim: Defective secretion of other molecules may cause diabetes mellitus and pubertas praecox.
source: Defective secretion of other molecules may cause diabetes mellitus and pubertas praecox.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as speculation.

claim: Endocrinological examination revealed that the glucose intolerance of the affected children is due to reduced levels of secreted insulin.
source: Endocrinological examination revealed that the glucose intolerance of the affected children is due to reduced levels of secreted insulin.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a finding from clinical examination.

claim: cTAGE5 is known to cooperate with TANGO1 in the mega cargo secretion pathway.
source: cTAGE5 is known to cooperate with TANGO1 in the mega cargo secretion pathway (Saito et al., 2011), but has also been shown to play a pivotal role in ER to Golgi trafficking of small molecules like proinsulin (Fan et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by citations.

claim: cTAGE5 has been shown to play a pivotal role in ER to Golgi trafficking of small molecules like proinsulin.
source: cTAGE5 is known to cooperate with TANGO1 in the mega cargo secretion pathway (Saito et al., 2011), but has also been shown to play a pivotal role in ER to Golgi trafficking of small molecules like proinsulin (Fan et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by a citation.

claim: The knockout of cTAGE5 in pancreatic β-cells resulted in defective islet structure, reduced insulin secretion, and severe glucose intolerance in mice.
source: The knockout of cTAGE5 in pancreatic β-cells resulted in defective islet structure, reduced insulin secretion, and severe glucose intolerance in mice (Fan et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by a citation.

claim: A correlation between TANGO1 phosphorylation and proinsulin trafficking in mouse pancreatic β-cells has recently been discovered.
source: Additionally, a correlation between TANGO1 phosphorylation and proinsulin trafficking in mouse pancreatic β-cells has recently been discovered (Kang et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by a citation.

claim: The investigated family presents the first TANGO1-associated syndrome in humans.
source: Collectively, the investigated family presents the first TANGO1-associated syndrome in humans, highlighting the role of fully functional TANGO1 in various disease pathways and bringing new potential target molecules of TANGO1 into focus.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a primary conclusion.
